title: EU proposes €50bn Sovereign Tech Equity Fund for AI and quantum
excerpt: The Financial Times reports Brussels is weighing a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund to cut reliance on US and Chinese technology.
content_html:
The European Commission has proposed a €50bn fund that would take direct stakes in European AI and quantum computing companies. The Sovereign Tech Equity Fund was confirmed on Wednesday, hours after the Financial Times first reported the plan, citing two officials.

The fund would make larger, riskier, and longer-term investments than the EU’s existing financing schemes. Its goal is to cut the bloc’s dependence on US and Chinese technology.

The legal basis for the fund sits inside the Quantum Act, which the Commission presented the same day in Strasbourg. Henna Virkkunen, the Commission’s tech chief, said the vehicle would reach beyond quantum to all technologies the EU deems critical.

“No company should be obliged to leave Europe due to lack of finance,” Virkkunen told reporters.

According to the FT, the money would flow into frontier technologies that matter for Europe’s industrial strength. The fund forms part of a wider push to keep strategic tech and supply chains on the continent.

Money has long been Europe’s sore spot, as the region attracts only around 5% of global venture capital flows, according to the FT’s report. EU officials worry that the continent’s best startups move abroad, or sell to foreign buyers, in search of growth capital.

The push follows the 2024 Draghi report, which urged the bloc to spend far more on innovation to keep up with the US and China.

The new vehicle would dwarf the schemes the EU already runs. Among them is the €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund, which is managed by private equity firm EQT and made its first investments this autumn, starting with Finnish satellite firm ICEYE. The Commission hopes to grow that fund to €25bn.

In 2023, the bloc also launched a €3.75bn fund of funds for late-stage startups. The European Investment Bank has drawn up its own plans to keep startups from leaving, and aims to mobilise €70bn for European tech by 2027 through its TechEU programme. The bank group says its Tech Champions funds now hold 15 unicorns.

European tech companies have pushed for something bigger. In March 2025, around 100 organisations wrote to Commission president Ursula von der Leyen calling for a sovereign infrastructure fund to back key technologies at home.

Henna Virkkunen, the Commission’s tech chief, told the FT last week that European quantum firms must be able to scale at home and that “big investments are needed.”
